Operator:
    Good morning, and welcome to the AeroTech Dynamics Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

    I would now like to turn the conference over to John Reynolds, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Reynolds:
    Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroTech Dynamics' Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Reyes, Chief Operating Officer; Nina Voss, Chief Technology Officer; and Greg Mills, Chief Strategy Officer.

    Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those discussed today.

David Harper:
    Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. AeroTech Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense systems, commercial aerospace, and space technologies. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our ATD-400 hypersonic glide vehicle program and its potential to accelerate our future growth trajectory. We are seeing strong demand for our precision strike and F-35 sustainment systems, while our commercial aerospace aftermarket business continues its steady recovery.

    With that, I'll turn it over to Emily to provide more details on our financial results and key operational highlights.

Emily Carter:
    Thank you, David, and good morning. I'm pleased to report that we delivered another quarter of strong execution against our strategic priorities, posting record revenue and expanding margins amid a resilient demand environment in both commercial aerospace and defense sectors.

    Starting with the top line, we reported Q2 revenue of $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 8% organically, exceeding our guidance midpoint. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, fueled by higher volume on mature defense programs, ramp-up on new awards, and sustained recovery in commercial aftermarket services.

    Breaking it down by segment: Defense Systems, which accounted for 62% of revenue, delivered $1.77 billion, a robust 18% year-over-year increase. Key contributors included accelerated deliveries on our Precision Strike portfolio, including the ATD-400 hypersonic glide vehicle variant, which saw a 25% volume uptick due to supplemental U.S. DoD funding tied to Ukraine aid packages. Our role as a Tier-1 supplier on the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program generated $450 million in Q2 bookings, with low-rate initial production Lot 16 ramping smoothly ahead of schedule. Margins here expanded 120 basis points to 13.8%, benefiting from favorable mix shift toward fixed-price contracts and supply chain efficiencies.

    Commercial Aerospace, 28% of revenue, reached $795 million, up 12% year-over-year, driven by aftermarket MRO demand as global fleets return to pre-pandemic utilization rates—now at 95% for narrowbody platforms like the Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo family. Our composite winglet upgrades and nacelle systems captured additional share, with OEM content growing 15% on long-term agreements with Boeing and Spirit AeroSystems.

    Space & Advanced Technologies, 10% of revenue, generated $285 million, flat year-over-year but with 20% sequential growth from our first major Space Force contract for reusable satellite bus platforms under the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture. Funded backlog now stands at a record $28.5 billion, up 22% year-over-year, with total backlog exceeding $45 billion—including $12 billion in options exercisable within 12 months. Our overall book-to-bill ratio of 1.3x reflects strong order inflow, particularly from international customers.

    Adjusted operating income rose 22% to $385 million, driving a 210 basis point expansion in segment operating margins to 13.5% overall. This was propelled by operational leverage—program cost efficiencies reduced Estimate at Completion adjustments to near-zero—and pricing discipline on commercial renewals. GAAP diluted EPS came in at $1.42, while adjusted EPS of $1.68 beat consensus by $0.09, supported by a 15% reduction in corporate G&A as a percentage of sales through digital transformation initiatives.

    Free cash flow was a standout at $420 million, or 109% of adjusted net income, bolstered by $250 million in advance payments on defense contracts and working capital normalization. Year-to-date, we've generated $750 million in operating cash flow, enabling $300 million in share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike announced today—our 15th consecutive annual increase.

    Strategically, we're capitalizing on geopolitical tailwinds and technological inflection points. Notable Q2 wins include a $1.2 billion IDIQ contract from the U.S. Army for next-gen counter-UAS systems, leveraging our AI-enabled drone swarm tech demonstrated at AUSA 2023; export approvals for ATD-400 missiles to NATO allies like Poland and Finland, adding $450 million to backlog amid heightened Eastern European tensions; and selection as prime for a DARPA hypersonics prototype, aligning with the DoD's $4.7 billion FY24 hypersonic R&D budget.

    Regionally, U.S. operations remain our bedrock, comprising 72% of revenue with DoD funding up 9% year-over-year per the latest NDAA. Europe drove 15% growth via F-35 sustainment and A400M workshares, while Asia-Pacific surged 28% on offsets for KF-21 fighter engines and growing MQ-9 Reaper demand from India and Australia—offsetting softer Middle East volumes due to temporary program pauses.

    On the technical front, our $450 million R&D investment, or 16% of sales, is yielding results: We've achieved TRL-7 on directed energy weapons for naval applications, partnering with Raytheon on HELIOS follow-ons, and launched a sustainable aviation fuel certification program for our nacelle liners, targeting 100% compatibility by 2026 to meet EU ETS mandates.

    We navigated headwinds like titanium supply constraints—now 80% resolved via dual-sourcing with VSMPO-AVISMA—and labor inflation, which we offset through 5% wage adjustments tied to productivity bonuses. No material program cost growth occurred, with our Enterprise Risk Management framework ensuring EACs remain stable.

    Building on these highlights, one of our key leading indicators is the book-to-bill ratio, both overall and by segment—a strong barometer of demand visibility and backlog momentum amid heightened geopolitical tensions, sustained U.S. DoD topline growth under the FY24 NDAA, and recovering commercial aftermarket dynamics.

    For the quarter, we delivered an overall book-to-bill ratio of 1.18x, up from 1.12x in Q2 2023 and sequentially from 1.15x in Q1 2024. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter above 1.0x, underscoring robust order intake across our portfolio. Total bookings reached $8.7 billion, outpacing revenue recognition of $2.85 billion. Year-to-date, we're at 1.16x, with bookings of $26.2 billion against $22.6 billion in revenue.

    This performance drove our total backlog to $142 billion overall when including all segments, up 8% year-over-year, with 42% funded. Unfunded backlog grew 12% to $38 billion, largely from IDIQ awards like the U.S. Army's LTAMDS radar follow-on and international F-35 sustainment contracts. This positions us for low double-digit organic revenue growth through 2026, with improving program mix favoring high-margin defense primes.

    Regionally, U.S. bookings comprised 68% of the total, fueled by DoD supplemental funding for Ukraine aid and Indo-Pacific deterrence. International orders, at 28%, surged 22% year-over-year, driven by Foreign Military Sales to NATO allies and Middle East partners—such as Poland's F-35 tranche 2 and Saudi Arabia's THAAD interceptors. Asia-Pacific contributed 15% of bookings, with early wins on hypersonic glide vehicle co-development under AUKUS Pillar II.

    By segment, Aeronautics, at 35% of revenue, posted a standout 1.25x ratio, with $3.2 billion in bookings versus $2.6 billion in revenue. Year-to-date, it's 1.22x. Key drivers included a $1.8 billion LRIP Lot 16 award for F-35 Lightning II aircraft—aligning with the program's $428 billion lifecycle value—and $950 million for B-21 Raider engineering change proposals. International F-35 orders from Finland and Switzerland added $400 million. Trends show sequential improvement, reflecting Next Generation Air Dominance digital engineering investments accelerating risk reduction milestones.

    Missiles and Fire Control, 28% of revenue, led with 1.32x—bookings of $2.9 billion against $2.2 billion revenue, the highest in three years. Highlights: $2.1 billion for Precision Strike Missiles and JASSM-ER, plus $550 million in hypersonic boosters under Conventional Prompt Strike. Geopolitical tailwinds from Ukraine replenishment and Taiwan Strait tensions boosted Pacific orders by 35%. Backlog here hit $42 billion, with 55% funded.

    Rotary and Mission Systems, 22% of revenue, came in at 1.05x, with $1.6 billion bookings versus $1.5 billion revenue. CH-53K full-rate production contracts at $800 million and MH-60R exports to India at $450 million offset softer upgrades. Middle East FMS grew 18%, tied to integrated air missile defense suites.

    Space, 15% of revenue, lagged at 0.95x—impacted by NASA SLS delays—but year-to-date at 1.02x, buoyed by Orion modules and GPS IIIF payloads. Trends are turning with proliferated LEO bids against SDA's Transport Layer Tranche 2.

    Overall, our book-to-bill trajectory reflects a favorable industry secular: DoD's $850 billion FY25 request and 5% global A&D market growth. We're prioritizing AI/ML for predictive logistics to sustain 1.2x+ ratios.

    As we turn to updated full-year guidance, we're raising the midpoint across key metrics, reflecting the strength of our backlog, robust program executions, and favorable tailwinds. Revenue is now guided to $11.4 billion to $11.7 billion, midpoint up 13% year-over-year, driven by higher-than-expected deliveries in defense and commercial aftermarket. Adjusted EPS to $6.75 to $7.00, with segment operating margins expanding to 12.0% to 12.5% via labor productivity and fixed-price settlements. Free cash flow to >105% conversion.

    U.S. DoD funding comprises 65% of revenues, with the FY24 NDAA's $886 billion topline providing visibility. International sales at 22%, led by Middle East and European offsets.

    Headwinds include commercial OEM softness and titanium volatility, but our $18 billion international pipeline mitigates.

    Before moving on, let's touch on aftermarket performance, which grew 22% year-over-year to represent a significant portion of our top line, with margins expanding due to its annuity-like nature. Globally, widebody and narrowbody utilization rates have rebounded to 82% across our installed base—up sharply post-pandemic. In commercial, PW1100G engines on A320neo hit 87% utilization, driving 1.2 million flight hours and higher shop visits. Defense fleets at 92%, with F-35 engines averaging 750 hours per tail.

    Asia-Pacific led at 89%, North America at 84%, EMEA at 78%. Maintenance cycles compressed, with time-on-wing at 22,000 hours, but our Engine Health Management system flagged 85% of issues pre-failure. Technical investments in digital twins, additive manufacturing, and TrueFleet subscriptions secure long-term growth, targeting 15-18% CAGR.

    On the defense budget outlook, it's a critical driver: The FY2025 request at $886 billion, up 4.1%, preserves RDT&E at $145 billion and procurement at $170 billion. Hypersonics up 12% to $4.7 billion benefits our LRASM and Glide Phase Interceptor programs. For us, this means tailwinds in missiles at $2.8 billion Q2 revenue, with backlog up 18%. Europe NATO spending and Asia-Pacific plans like Japan's $320 billion enhance our positioning. Risks like CRs are mitigated by our 36-month backlog coverage. This supports our raised FY25 outlook and ROIC above 15%.

    Finally, on key programs: In NGAD subsystems, we've completed Phase 2A testing with 28% improved accuracy, ramping LRIP to 8 kits monthly; backlog $2.8 billion. Precision Strike delivered 156 JATM rounds, 19% up, with $4.1 billion backlog. MQ-Next CCA achieved first flight, unlocking $320 million funding. GMD upgrades hit 100% intercept success, with $2.4 billion backlog. Commercial 787 spars up 14%. Total program backlogs $18.5 billion, up 12%, guiding 10-12% FY25 growth.

    Gross margin was 28.5%, operating income $385 million, free cash flow $420 million. Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Guidance for the full year remains on track with these updates, and we're actively managing costs while investing in growth and returning capital via dividends and repurchases.

Tom Reyes:
    Thank you, Emily. Operationally, we've seen significant improvements in supply chain management, resolving 80% of titanium constraints through dual-sourcing and increasing production rates on key F-35 and ATD-400 programs. We're investing in automation, digital twins, and predictive analytics to boost efficiency, reduce EACs, and shorten turnaround times—now at 45 days for F-35 overhauls—while enhancing mission-capable rates.

Nina Voss:
    Thank you, Tom. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion and sensor fusion, achieving TRL-7 on directed energy weapons with Raytheon and quantum signal processing for NGAD. Our AI-driven drone swarms and hypersonic seekers, tested at Mach 5+, give us a competitive edge, supported by $450 million in R&D for SAF compatibility and reusable space platforms.

Operator:
    Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Lawson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lawson:
    Good morning. Can you provide more color on the book-to-bill ratio trends by segment and how they inform your multi-year outlook?

David Harper:
    Certainly, Mike. As Emily detailed, our overall 1.18x reflects strength across the board, with Missiles at 1.32x from JASSM and hypersonics, and Aeronautics at 1.25x via F-35 LRIP. This >1.1x trajectory, bolstered by DoD supplementals and international FMS, supports low double-digit growth through 2026, with backlog visibility at 3.5 years mitigating risks.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
    Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the drivers behind aftermarket strength, particularly fleet utilization and any MRO cycle shifts?

Emily Carter:
    Sarah, great question. Utilization at 82-92% globally is compressing maintenance cycles, boosting shop visits 18-20%. Our EHM analytics and AM parts cut costs 25%, driving 22% growth and 37% margins. Defense PBL contracts and commercial TrueFleet take-rates ensure annuity revenue, with Q4 at $2.9-3.1 billion.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
    Regarding updates on key programs like NGAD and hypersonics—any milestones or production risks?

Nina Voss:
    Alex, we've hit key milestones: NGAD Phase 2A testing with 28% accuracy gains, JATM 156 deliveries up 19%, and MQ-Next first flight unlocking funding. Supply chains are 92% derisked, with capex driving margin expansion to 16.5% on scale—positioned for FY25 FRP decisions.

David Harper:
    Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities—hypersonics, uncrewed systems, and space resilience—operational excellence, and innovation in this multi-year upcycle.

John Reynolds:
    Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q2 Fiscal 2024 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
    This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
